title: ltestats v1

data.$comment: A CLOSED enumeration of two shapes (DL-146, 18 Sep 2026): the modem reports either a measurement or the reason it has none. A record that is neither - or both halves at once - dead-letters, exactly as an unknown fourth lorastats dialect does (DL-105 rule 4).

rsrp.$comment: OPTIONAL since 18 Sep 2026 (DL-146), as is rsrq: both are LTE reference-signal measurements, and a modem that has fallen back to 2G reports neither. 5 of 300 live records carried access_Technology "2G" with rssi/plmn/imsi/operator/lac/cid and nothing else; requiring them dead-lettered every degraded modem - the record ops most needs - which is the trap Q4a found in netstats.

access_Technology.$comment: NOTE THE CAPITAL T. Production sends access_Technology. Every document in this repository said access_technology before 29 Aug 2026; that spelling came from the SRS and has never appeared on the wire. Under ADR-007 production is the authoritative wire format, so the capital is correct and the lowercase spelling is the bug.

imsi.$comment: Sensitive identifier. Charset is constrained but length is deliberately not: rejecting a valid IMSI on a guessed length would dead-letter real traffic. Stored raw; the read API returns it masked (D-12 P3, decided 12 Oct 2026, DL-167). This rule must stay digits-only: the masking and the OpenAPI drift gate are written against it.

shapeUnknownTechnology.title: unknown-technology

etxt.$comment: Free-text reason the modem produced no measurement. Observed value: "unknown technology".

shapeUnknownTechnology.$comment: A modem that never registered sends data: {"etxt": "unknown technology"} and no measurement at all (1 of 300 live records, 18 Sep 2026). Closed on purpose - additionalProperties false - so that etxt NEXT TO a partial measurement matches neither shape and dead-letters: half a measurement is not a known shape.

signedNumericString.$comment: Signal values are STRINGS on the wire - production sends "rssi": "-67", not -67. Constrained to an optionally-signed integer so a non-numeric value dead-letters at the Writer rather than failing a cast at query time. The Writer parses to BIGINT and MUST range-check before conversion.

hexString.$comment: lac and cid are hexadecimal strings (55F3, 61D93D, 28DC413). Width is left generous on purpose; only the charset is asserted.

$comment: Re-derived from the 29 Aug 2026 production sample (ADR-007). TWO corrections against the previous SRS-derived draft, each of which alone dead-lettered 100% of ltestats traffic: every numeric is a STRING on the wire, not an integer; and the field is access_Technology with a capital T. timespan is optional - one of the three production records omits it. 18 Sep 2026 (DL-146): data is a closed oneOf of two shapes, re-derived from 1,980 live records - rsrp/rsrq are optional (absent on 2G) and an etxt-only record from a modem that never registered is valid.
